title: Beni Mellal city and foothills on 20 Oct 2026
summary: On 20 Oct 2026 the radar shows Beni Mellal city and its foothills inside a 6 km circle, where built-up land covers 12.2% and trees, shrub and rugged slopes 52.5%. This date carries a flag for a backscatter shift, so its values are less reliable than those of an unflagged date.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: Built-up land reaches 7.14 dB in HH, and the circle averages -0.72 dB in HH and -13.1 dB in HV. Every type is bright on this date, smooth bare ground included, at -13.28 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Built-up land, 13.75 km2, has an HV:HH ratio of -17.48 dB, the double-bounce signature of walls. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes, 59.32 km2, give HV of -12.28 dB from leaves and branches. Rough dry ground and fields sit at -8.83 dB in HH. Changing fields, 4.8%, are at -14.54 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: One flag applies: backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median, a possible processing offset or widespread wet conditions. Possible cause: a processing offset; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: rain wetting soil and walls; rain records would check it. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow.
